newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - First day FOMC, NAPM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - First day FOMC, NAPM.

text.p: The Federal Reserve's policy-making arm will convene in Washington on Tuesday for the first leg of a two-day meeting, but a key report on manufacturing conditions will take center stage for the U.S. Treasury market, experts said.

"People will obviously focus on the (manufacturing) number," said Cary Leahey, chief U.S. economist at High Frequency Economics. "Even if the number is strong, it's not going to affect the Fed's decision-making process this week."
The National Asociation of Purchasing Management will issue its June report on manufacturing at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.
U.S. economists in a Reuters survey conducted last Friday expected a reading of 56.4 for June compared to 57.1 in May.
A reading above 50.0 indicates an expanding manufacturing economy, according to NAPM.
Leahey said a robust manufacturing sector as portrayed by the NAPM, coupled with solid employment growth last month could prompt a change in Treasury market psychology.
"People will say ... maybe the economy is rebounding a bit in June," he said. "So the risk is that the market may start rethinking its view on the Fed not for July, but for August," he added.

Mark Mahoney, Treasury strategist at Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette Securities Corp, predicted a strong NAPM report for Tuesday, but noted any reaction could be contained because the market began pricing in a robust report on Monday.
"We priced part of it in with (Monday's move), so that should keep the market from blowing apart," he said.
Still, Mahoney said the long bond could begin climbing toward a 6.85 percent yield as early as Tuesday.
On Monday, the benchmark 30-year U.S. government security closed 1/2-point lower at 97-31/32 to yield 6.78 percent. On Friday, the bond yielded 6.75 percent.
"If the NAPM comes in a couple points above the high-end of expectations, it's probably going to be another selloff," added Jonathan Basile, an economist at HSBC Markets Inc.

Analysts said the manufacturing sector has been catching market attention in recent weeks as recent data showed stubborn strength in that sector. This comes despite signs of cooling in consumer spending.
"If we are going to get an (economic) slowdown in the second half of the year, (the market) will have to look at the industrial sector and not the consumer sector," Basile said.
Speaking of the consumer sector, on Tuesday the market will also get the latest retail sales data from BTM/Schroders and Lynch, Jones and Ryan Inc. The figures will be for the week of June 28.
In the preivous periods, the reports showed an unchanged reading and a 1.6-percnet advance, respectively.
Data on construction spending and leading economic indicators both for May will be less significant, market sources said.
The Federal Open Market Committee is expected to kick off the first day of its two-day confab at 0900 EDT/1300 GMT.
